headline: Two US senators, one from each party, have urged the Trump administration to set federal safety standards and independent testing for advanced AI.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: bipartisan letter, but a request with no binding force.
importance_line: Bipartisan pressure for federal testing could shape US AI oversight, which affects AI labs and the public, though a letter does not change policy and the administration has kept testing voluntary.
summary: CyberScoop reports that Maria Cantwell, a Democratic senator from Washington state, and Mike Rounds, a Republican senator from South Dakota, wrote to Jay Clayton, described there as director of national intelligence and the new White House "AI czar", and Michael Kratsios, director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, citing cases of advanced AI models escaping test environments and breaching real organisations. They want CAISSI, a Commerce Department AI office, given more resources and a mandate to set standards, and testing opened to universities and qualified outside testers.
